rationale:
bugs_open/329: both takeover arms of handleOrchestrationStatus decide an orchestration is stuck by a CLOCK (time.Since(state.LastActivity) > StuckOrchestrationTimeout, 300s) and then resume it with nothing claiming the row. Raised by the council's own guardian seat on migration 465's round (corr 1c212b15, APPROVED) and filed because an objection living only inside a verdict is invisible.

TWO PREMISES IN THE BUG FILE ARE FALSE AND I AM CORRECTING THEM RATHER THAN BUILDING ON THEM. (1) The file states [MEASURED 2026-08-19] that SetExecutingStep/ClearExecutingStep 'end in r.UpdateState — NOT UpdateStateWithVersion, so the write does no version check'. state.go:883-885 is a one-line wrapper: 'func (r *StateRepository) UpdateState(ctx, state) error { return r.UpdateStateWithVersion(ctx, state, state.Version) }'. UpdateState IS the version CAS, so the file's fix candidate (2) is a NO-OP. (2) I myself wrote, and have retracted in the file, that every agent binary runs the arms; only cmd/agent-chassis imports platform/agentbase.

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT A MISSING GUARD ON THE WRITE. It is a CHECK-THEN-ACT ACROSS TWO READS: the arm judges staleness on the CALLER'S SNAPSHOT (coordinator.go:761, :796), and the write that follows does a FRESH GetState -> mutate -> CAS that never re-evaluates the predicate. Two takers seconds apart both win, because each CASes against the version it just read. Corollary that inverts the obvious test: exactly-SIMULTANEOUS takers do NOT double-execute today (the loser's CAS fails), so a WaitGroup start-line test shows the unfixed code passing. The disconfirming case is the SEQUENTIAL interleaving.

HONEST SIZING, BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENTS DO NOT SUPPORT A LARGER CHANGE. This is a correctness gap, not a fire. The dispatch_throughput lane's double-handle census over 24h [MEASURED 2026-09-03 ~11:4xZ]: 3,044 handler orchestrations, 2,911 distinct work items, 71 items with >=2 handlers, and 0 overlapping pairs on one item. 0 rows with a repeated step name in one execution_path over 7d. 0 'Found stuck orchestration' / 'stalled between steps' lines in either chassis pod's reachable log window. There are THREE guards in series and the defect sits in the middle of them: (i) the chassis intake serialisation claim, keyed on orchestration_id, agent-chassis ONLY; (ii) THE ARMS, the defect; (iii) per-path CASes such as the work-item claim on the dispatch path. Guards (i) and (iii) absorb the outcome where they apply.

WHY FIX IT ANYWAY, STATED AS WHAT IT REMOVES RATHER THAN WHAT IT PREVENTS TODAY: the absorption is a BY-PRODUCT. Guard (iii) exists to make work-item claiming exclusive and protects this defect by accident; a refactor could remove it without knowing it was load-bearing. Guard (i) is disabled STRUCTURALLY for spawned pods (intake.go refuses the mode when a.spawned) - and spawned Job pods of the chassis image are the MAJORITY of orchestration drivers: processing_node over 14d [MEASURED 2026-09-03 ~11:3xZ] gives agent-chassis 3,332 against 4,900+ from agent-page-rerender 2,215, agent-build-dispatch-loop 660, agent-page-build-handler 412 and 9 more families, every one confirmed absent from kubectl get deploy. That census could have come out agent-chassis:100% and did not.

THE DESIGN IS THE MINIMAL ONE AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLOSE EVERYTHING. Move the staleness decision INSIDE the version-guarded write, composed from the existing ExecuteWithOptimisticLocking plus a sentinel. No new SQL, no new column, no touch on processing_node - so the council invariant that orchestration_states' two guarded mechanisms must never share a column (state_locks_test.go, corr 4a227ed9) is preserved trivially: the new method contains no UPDATE literal at all. What it makes unrepresentable: N takers resuming one stale row. What it does NOT close: a live driver versus one taker - defaultLocalActionTimeout is 7200s (coordinator.go:1246) and NOTHING refreshes last_activity during a local action, so a driver inside a 9-minute council seat is 'stuck' by a 5-minute clock while behaving correctly. No claim taken by the takeover side can exclude a driver that holds nothing; closing that needs a driver heartbeat, which is a separate seam I am deliberately not carrying. Post-fix bound per orchestration: 2 (driver + exactly one taker), from unbounded.

NOT ARCHITECTURE-SCOPE by the 2026-07-29 §1 test: the shared mechanism's guarantee is NARROWED (an unconditional resume becomes a claimed one), not widened. No opt-in field per 2026-08-02 §2: the fix REMOVES authority from a branch, no caller-supplied predicate licenses a widest branch, and no action input spec changes (RFC_022's N=10 optional-key budget untouched). A 'revert to clock-only' switch would be a mechanism rotting unexercised, which 2026-07-29 §2 declines to require. ExecuteWithOptimisticLocking has ZERO non-test callers today; this gives it its first, and the tests exercise its conflict-retry path.

plan.summary: A takeover is CLAIMED, never ASSUMED. Move the arms' staleness predicate from the caller's snapshot into the version-guarded write, so judging and claiming are one atomic step. The winner's write bumps version and refreshes last_activity, so every later taker's fresh read declines. Composed from existing machinery only: ExecuteWithOptimisticLocking + a sentinel error. No new SQL, no new column, processing_node untouched.

edits.rationale: A typed 'lost the claim' outcome the arm can distinguish from a DB error. Without it the arm cannot tell 'another actor is driving this' (return nil, drop the message, exactly as the existing non-stale branch does) from 'the database is broken' (propagate).
edits.sketch:
var (
 	ErrWaitingForResponse   = errors.New("orchestration is waiting for responses")
 	ErrVersionMismatch      = errors.New("optimistic lock failure: version mismatch")
 	ErrLoopExpansionHandled = errors.New("loop expansion handled: outer continueExecution must not continue")
+	// ErrTakeoverLost: the row this caller judged stale from its SNAPSHOT was no
+	// longer stale on the FRESH read inside the claim -- another actor resumed it,
+	// or it moved on. The caller returns without executing anything (bugs_open/329).
+	ErrTakeoverLost = errors.New("stale-orchestration takeover lost: the row is being driven")
 )

edits.rationale: The check-and-claim primitive. The caller judged the row stuck from a SNAPSHOT; this re-judges it on the FRESH row INSIDE the version CAS and writes only if it is still stale. The write IS the claim -- UpdateStateWithVersion already stamps last_activity=now and version+1 unconditionally, so the next caller's fresh read sees a row that is no longer stale. A lost version race is re-read by ExecuteWithOptimisticLocking and RE-JUDGED, never retried blind. Contains no UPDATE literal of its own, so state_locks_test.go's setClauseOf never sees it and the two-guarded-mechanisms invariant is untouched.

One call site for both arms, with named log needles (STALE_TAKEOVER_CLAIMED / STALE_TAKEOVER_LOST) that are the post-roll field meters -- there is no durable needle today, which is why 'have the arms ever fired?' is currently unanswerable beyond the log window. Returns nil on a lost claim, not an error: the message was for an orchestration another actor is driving, which is exactly the outcome of the arms' existing non-stale branch.
The snapshot saying 'stuck' becomes a reason to TRY a takeover, not to perform one. Replaces ClearExecutingStep + reload + continueExecution, whose three separate reads are the check-then-act.

The RUNNING arm previously wrote NOTHING at all before resuming, so two arrivals seconds apart both resumed. The long explanatory comment above it is kept; only its stale reference to ClearExecutingStep needs adjusting.

Its SOLE caller was the arm being replaced (repo-wide grep 2026-09-03: coordinator.go:765 plus one comment reference at :781). A helper with no callers reads as a finished refactor, which this estate has been bitten by before. SetExecutingStep is untouched -- it retains callers at :746 and :896.

Written to reference ONLY pre-existing symbols so it compiles and RUNS RED against unfixed HEAD -- the bug file demands the positive test be watched to fail first. sqlmock (the package's established pattern) fails on any unexpected statement, so the expectation list IS the complete DB traffic of the span, which is how the arm is isolated from the guards in series above and below it. Includes the negative control (a fresh row must be taken over by NEITHER arm) in the same run, so a fix that refuses everything cannot pass.

TestStaleExecutingStepTakeoverIsRefusedWhenTheFreshRowIsBeingDriven: snapshot EXECUTING_STEP/idle 6m/v7;
mock returns fresh row (last_activity=now, v9) and expects NO Exec. Unfixed HEAD: ClearExecutingStep issues
an UPDATE, sqlmock rejects it, the arm errors -> RED, and the message names the resume that must not have happened.

TestStaleRunningResumeIsRefusedWhenTheFreshRowIsBeingDriven: same for the RUNNING arm.
TestSimultaneousTakersOnlyOneClaims: ExpectExec -> RowsAffected 0 (other taker won), reload -> fresh, assert nil.
TestStaleTakeoverClaimsAndResumesWhenNobodyElseHas: POSITIVE CONTROL -- claim succeeds, assert the sentinel
error from continueExecution's first read proves it was entered, and processing_history carries stale_takeover_claimed.
TestFreshRowsAreNeverTakenOver: NEGATIVE CONTROL, both arms, mock expects NOTHING.

edits.rationale: Pins ClaimStaleOrchestration's four refusal arms directly, so a later edit that loosens the predicate fails here rather than silently widening what can be taken over: refuses a fresh row; refuses a status mismatch; refuses EXECUTING_STEP with CurrentlyExecuting == nil; and returns the bumped version on a win.

grounded_in: platform/orchestration/coordinator.go:761 (EXECUTING_STEP arm): 'if state.CurrentlyExecuting != nil && time.Since(state.LastActivity) > StuckOrchestrationTimeout {' -- followed by ClearExecutingStep, a fresh GetState, and continueExecution, none of which re-tests the predicate.

platform/orchestration/coordinator.go:796 (RUNNING arm): 'if time.Since(state.LastActivity) > StuckOrchestrationTimeout {' -- followed directly by 'return s.continueExecution(ctx, state, execCtx)', writing NOTHING before resuming.

platform/orchestration/state.go:883-885: 'func (r *StateRepository) UpdateState(ctx context.Context, state *OrchestrationState) error { return r.UpdateStateWithVersion(ctx, state, state.Version) }' -- REFUTES bugs_open/329's [MEASURED 2026-08-19] claim that these writes do no version check, and makes its fix candidate (2) a no-op.

platform/orchestration/state.go:1378-1380 (TakeOverOrchestration doc): 'It deliberately leaves `version` alone: this is bookkeeping, not a state transition, and must never collide with UpdateStateWithVersion's optimistic lock.' -- why candidate (1), routing the arms through that CAS, is the wrong primitive here.

platform/orchestration/state_locks_test.go header: 'orchestration_states has TWO guarded-update mechanisms and they must never govern the same column ... If either ever writes the other's columns, two locks race on one field and neither is authoritative.' -- the invariant this design preserves by containing no UPDATE literal at all.

platform/orchestration/coordinator.go:1246: 'defaultLocalActionTimeout = 7200 * time.Second' with every last_activity refresh site (:1039,:2220,:2850,:2914,:3441,:3975) being a step transition -- so a live driver inside a long step is 'stuck' by a 300s clock, and this is the residual the fix explicitly does NOT close.

platform/agentbase/intake.go:75 and :215-224: the intake serialisation claim is refused when a.spawned, and keys on the orchestration_id -- so the guard that absorbs this defect on static chassis pods is structurally absent on spawned Job pods.

dispatch_throughput lane's double-handle census [MEASURED 2026-09-03 ~11:4xZ]: 3,044 handlers, 2,911 items, 71 items with >=2 handlers, 0 overlapping pairs on one item -- the honest bound: this is a correctness gap, not a fire, and the fix is sized as one.
plan.risks:
1) THE OBVIOUS TEST IS INVERTED, so a careless reviewer or a later maintainer will 'prove' the unfixed code correct. Exactly-simultaneous takers do NOT double-execute today -- the loser's version CAS fails and the arm returns the error. The disconfirming case is the SEQUENTIAL interleaving (taker A wins and refreshes last_activity; taker B arrives seconds later on a stale snapshot). Both test files are written around the sequential case and say so in their headers.

2) A GUARD IN SERIES CAN PASS THE TEST FOR ME. There are three layers: the chassis intake serialisation claim above, the arms, and per-path CASes below (the work-item claim on the dispatch path). Any verification on the dispatch path is worthless -- guard (iii) absorbs a double-takeover even with the fix reverted. The tests call handleOrchestrationStatus directly, below the intake claim and above any action-level CAS, and sqlmock's reject-on-unexpected-statement makes the expectation list the complete DB traffic of the span.

3) BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE VISIBLE TO OTHERS: a message arriving at a stale row that another actor has just resumed is now DROPPED with STALE_TAKEOVER_LOST (return nil, offset committed) instead of resumed. This is the same disposition as the existing non-stale branch, so it is not a new class of drop -- but if the claim predicate were ever wrong in the refusing direction, recovery of genuinely abandoned rows would silently stop. That is what the positive control test exists for, and why the CLAIMED needle is logged at Warn.

4) WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, stated so no one reads more into it: driver-versus-taker. defaultLocalActionTimeout is 7200s and nothing refreshes last_activity during a local action, so a live driver on a 9-minute step is 'stuck' by the 300s clock. No claim on the takeover side can exclude a driver that holds nothing. Post-fix bound is 2 (driver + one taker), down from unbounded. Closing it needs a driver heartbeat -- a separate seam, deliberately not carried here.

5) ExecuteWithOptimisticLocking gains its FIRST non-test caller (0 today, grep 2026-09-03). Its retry loop is 12 attempts; a hot row could in principle exhaust them, which surfaces as an error rather than a double-execution -- the safe direction. The tests exercise the conflict-retry path explicitly.

6) NOT MINE TO TOUCH: claim_work_item_action.go (another lane's seam, now carrying an opt-in honour_spend_governor pre-claim read) and intake_workers.go (the 180s lease). Neither is in the edit list. The 180s-lease-vs-300s-timeout ordering is recorded as a finding in bugs_open/329 §5; the dispatch_throughput lane was offered it and declined it on the ground that they have never measured it, so it is attributed to nobody.
